candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

The Most High addresses Enoch directly: 'Fear not, Enoch, thou righteous man and scribe of righteousness: approach hither and hear my voice.' This is the dominical commissioning of Enoch as 'the scribe of righteousness' — the title that becomes Enoch's canonical Tewahedo designation. The address establishes Enoch as the prototype of the prophetic scribe: not an autonomous voice but an inspired recorder, and not a recorder of human history but of divine self-revelation. The Tewahedo Synaxarium honors Enoch on the 27th of Hidar specifically as scribe-of-righteousness, with this verse appointed for liturgical reading.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36)
candidates.source_attribution: 1 Enoch 15:8-10, trans. R.H. Charles (1912). PD. Cf. Mk 1:23-27.
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) (c. 200 BC)

Of the giants born from the Watcher-human unions: 'But now the giants, who are produced from the spirits and flesh, shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling' — the foundational Enochic etiology of demons. The giants (Nephilim) die in the Flood; their disembodied spirits become the unclean spirits that the New Testament accounts will exorcise. This is the Tewahedo demonological tradition's textual root: demons are not eternally-fallen lower angels but specifically the disembodied spirits of the antediluvian giants. The exorcistic ministry of Christ (cf. Mk 1:23-27 + parallels) presupposes this Enochic understanding.
